title: Exploratory cohort study on the influence of viral infections (infectious mononucleosis, SARS-CoV-2, influenza) on the development of neurological diseases in children and young adults
summary: Viruses can also cause children, teenagers and young adults to become acutely and seriously ill. Fever, a cough and a runny nose, as well as acute physical exhaustion, are the most common symptoms. Almost all children make a full recovery after an infection. However, some develop long-term complications months – and in some cases even years – later. Long COVID syndrome, which is associated with symptoms such as chronic fatigue, impaired sense of smell and taste, and difficulties concentrating and sleeping, is currently one of the best-known conditions affecting children, adolescents and young adults. These symptoms, which are also grouped under the term ‘chronic fatigue syndrome’, can also occur following infection with other viruses, such as the Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) or influenza. Scientific studies to date have already shown that viral diseases such as SARS-CoV-2, influenza and infectious mononucleosis (IM) are associated with an increased risk of disorders of the nervous and immune systems. It is considered that the viruses responsible for these infections remain in the body and alter the the immune system in such a way that, in a small number of people, can lead to disturbances in nerve function or to chronic inflammatory (autoimmune) diseases, such as multiple sclerosis. One question that has not yet been answered, however, is what role age plays in acute infection. The aim of this study is to investigate the working of the immune system during and after infection with influenza, COVID-19 (SARS-CoV-2) and infectious mononucleosis. Our aim is to establish a link between acute infection with these viruses – in particular IM – and the development of long-term (chronic) conditions affecting the nervous and/or immune systems, such as multiple sclerosis. In the long term, this should help to improve treatments for these chronic diseases and to develop preventive measures, such as vaccinations. Over the five-year observation period, we will learn how infection spreads within families and whether living conditions and/or underlying health conditions have an influence on this.
conditions: acute infectious diseases caused by influenza, SARS-CoV-2, Epstein-Barr virus, HHV-6 and CMV

interventions.name: It is an exploratory cohort study with a recruitment period of 5 years. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
·Signed and dated informed consent form of the legal guardian (and optional from the child)
·Known infectious mononucleosis, SARS-CoV2 or influenza infection
Exclusion criteria:
•	Missing informed consent
•	Known chronic illness 
1.	Immunodeficiency (primary or secondary (e.g. HIV))
2.	Severe global developmental retardation
3.	Diseases associated with increased inflammation (e.g. Crohn's disease, cystic fibrosis)
•	Other confirmed infectious diseases (e.g. hepatitis, tuberculosis)
•	pregnancy
